# 5. Deployment {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #00C9A7)"}

Taking it to production.

## Exporting Models

A PyTorch `.pt` file is great for research, but slow in production.
Convert to optimized formats using the `export` mode!

::: {.panel-tabset}

### CLI
```bash
# Export to ONNX (Great for CPU)
yolo export model=best.pt format=onnx

# Export to OpenVINO (Intel) or TensorRT (Nvidia GPUs)
yolo export model=best.pt format=openvino
```

### Python
```python
from ultralytics import YOLO

model = YOLO("best.pt")
model.export(format="onnx")
model.export(format="openvino")
```

:::

*Docs Reference: [Export](https://docs.ultralytics.com/modes/export/)*

## Inference with Exported Models

You don't need complex deployment code to use your exported models. The Ultralytics API loads them just like a standard PyTorch `.pt` file!

::: {.panel-tabset}

### CLI
```bash
yolo predict model=best.onnx source="https://ultralytics.com/assets/bus.jpg"
```

### Python
```python
from ultralytics import YOLO

model = YOLO("best.onnx")
results = model.predict(source="https://ultralytics.com/assets/bus.jpg")
print(results[0].boxes) 
```

:::

*Docs Reference: [Predict with Exported Models](https://docs.ultralytics.com/modes/predict/)*


## Deployment Strategies

Where your model lives depends on your application's requirements.

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
### ☁️ Cloud
*   **Scale**: Handle millions of requests.
*   **Ease**: Managed GPUs (AWS, GCP).
*   **Tooling**: Kubernetes, Ray Serve.
*   *Best for: SaaS, Web Apps.*
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### 📱 Edge / Local
*   **Latency**: Real-time response (<30ms).
*   **Privacy**: Data never leaves the device.
*   **Offline**: Works without internet.
*   *Best for: Robotics, Mobile, Security.*
:::
:::

## Model Optimization: Quantization

Moving from **FP32** (Training) to **FP16** or **INT8** can provide massive speedups.

| Precision | Model Size | Theoretical Speed | Relative Accuracy |
|-----------|------------|-------------------|-------------------|
| **FP32**  | 100%       | 1x (Baseline)     | 100% (Baseline)   |
| **FP16**  | ~50%       | ~2x               | Minimal / No Loss |
| **INT8**  | ~25%       | ~4x+              | 1-3% Typical Drop |

::: {.callout-note}
Actual gains depend heavily on your target hardware (e.g., NVIDIA Tensor Cores vs. Apple Neural Engine) and your calibration dataset.
:::

```python
# Export with half-precision or INT8 quantization
model.export(format="engine", half=True)     # TensorRT FP16
model.export(format="engine", int8=True)     # TensorRT INT8
```

## Benchmarking Performance

Don't guess the performance—measure it on your target hardware.

```python
from ultralytics.utils.benchmarks import benchmark

# Benchmark on current hardware across multiple formats
benchmark(model="yolo26n.pt", data="coco8.yaml", device="cpu")
```

**Metrics included:**
*   **Inference time (ms)** per image.
*   **Throughput (FPS)**.
*   **Model Size (MB)**.
*   **ONNX, OpenVINO, TensorRT** comparisons.

## Docker & Containerization

Avoid "it works on my machine" issues by using standardized environments.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Pull Image
```bash
# Get the official Ultralytics image with GPU support
docker pull ultralytics/ultralytics:latest-python
```

### Run Container
```bash
# Run inference inside a container
docker run -it --ipc=host --gpus all ultralytics/ultralytics \
  yolo predict model=yolo26n.pt source='https://ultralytics.com/images/bus.jpg'
```

:::

*Docs Reference: [Docker Guide](https://docs.ultralytics.com/guides/docker-quickstart/)*


## Edge & Mobile Deployment

Ultralytics supports a wide range of hardware-specific formats.

*   **NVIDIA Jetson**: TensorRT (`.engine`)
*   **Apple (iPhone/Mac)**: CoreML (`.mlpackage`)
*   **Android / IoT**: TFLite (`.tflite`)
*   **Web Browsers**: TensorFlow.js / ONNX.js
*   **Vision Sensors**: Sony IMX500 (Raspberry Pi AI Camera).

> **Pro Tip**: Use the `half=True` or `int8=True` argument when exporting for mobile to keep the app size small!

## Production Best Practices

To ensure a smooth transition from development to the real world:

1.  **Warm-up**: Run 1-2 dummy inferences to initialize hardware/drivers before processing live data.
2.  **Environment Parity**: Match your production OS/Drivers to your testing environment (use Docker!).
3.  **Input Validation**: Ensure production images are the same resolution as training (e.g., `imgsz=640`).
4.  **Monitoring**: Log inference times and confidence scores to detect **Data Drift**.

## Ultralytics HUB 🚀

The all-in-one platform for no-code model management.

*   **Cloud Training**: Track experiments without managing GPUs.
*   **Dataset Management**: Label and version your data.
*   **One-Click Deployment**: Deploy models directly to iOS and Android apps using the HUB App.
*   **API Access**: Managed endpoints for your custom models.

*Check it out at [hub.ultralytics.com](https://hub.ultralytics.com)*
